#### New Kenosha hub significantly expands G10 Fulfillment’s Midwest warehouse capacity

 Posted in Kenosha County Economic Development 

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

G10 Fulfillment now occupies 315,000 square feet of a 600,000-square-foot building at 12345 38th St., just off Interstate 94. The move increases G10’s dock capacity to 65 doors from 30.

“The Midwest is probably the most important hub for us,” said co-founder and CEO Mark Becker, who was on hand Thursday for a ribbon-cutting at the facility. He pointed to the region’s freight infrastructure and its location along the trucking corridor between Chicago and Milwaukee.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

Cargo Lift Solutions Leases 37,000 SF Warehouse in Medley

# Logistics Newcomer Secures Its First South Florida Foothold 

October 14, 2026/ in Industrial / Flex, Industry News, Miami-Dade County Industrial / Flex, NA / by CRE-sources Editorial Staff / 

Cargo Lift Solutions has leased 37,000 square feet at Prologis Palmetto Tradeport, located at 8090 NW 77th Court in Medley, for its first facility. The air cargo logistics company signed a five-year agreement with landlord Prologis and occupied the industrial space in September 2026. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Fausto Commercial’s Kodiak Fields and Ben Kunzle represented the tenant. JLL’s Ana Rivera represented Prologis.

The space offers 24-foot clear heights, 12 dock doors and one drive-in door. Airport proximity and highway access position the facility to connect air freight with truck distribution.

The commitment comes as Miami-Dade industrial vacancy declined to 6.5% in the third quarter, according to Colliers.

# 3PL Arvato opens its seventh logistics facility in Louisville 

400,000 square foot site takes Arvato’s total Louisville footprint beyond four million square feet.

By DC Velocity Staff Oct 05, 2026

DC Velocity Staff See Full Bio 

The supply chain management and e-commerce third party logistics provider (3PL) Arvato has opened its seventh logistics facility in Louisville, Kentucky, saying the move further expands its presence in one of the United States’ most important logistics hubs.

The new, wholly-owned site adds approximately 400,000 square feet of capacity, taking Arvato’s total Louisville footprint beyond four million square feet. Expected to create approximately 150 new jobs, the facility further strengthens the company’s ability to support growing fulfillment and distribution requirements for clients across North America, Arvato said.

According to Germany-based Arvato, brands need supply chain solutions that can support growth without adding complexity, whether they are entering new markets, managing rising order volumes, or optimizing delivery performance.
